shipped.warum: Where the quarrel begins, from Palacký's Documenta (1869), read against the page images with a working translation: the king gives the Bohemian nation three votes at the university of Prague, the three other nations petition and swear to leave, and a Bohemian master defends the decree: 'the head and not the tail', and 'I am the truth, not the custom'.

shipped.kurz: Peter of Mladoňovice: the trial and death of Hus
shipped.warum: The eyewitness account of Hus's party, from Palacký's Documenta (1869), read against the page images with a working translation: Sigismund's safe conduct, the arrest of 28 November 1414, the king's words at the hearings of June 1415 ('do not believe him if he recants'), the sentence, the degradation and the burning of 6 July.

Six letters, from the arrival without safe conduct to the eve of the end, in the original Latin or Czech from Palacký (1869) with Workman and Pope's English (1904): the gaolers' flight, the king's word 'as little to be trusted as the safe-conduct', why he cannot abjure, 'God will raise up braver men', and 'Sigismund hath acted deceitfully throughout'.

shipped.kurz: The king's word and the council's (1415)
shipped.warum: From Palacký's Documenta, read against the page images with a working translation: Sigismund revokes every safe conduct he gave at Constance (8 April 1415); 250 lords write to him in Czech that Hus was 'seized under your safe conduct' and that no one will trust his safe conducts again (12 May); and the council explains to Bohemia why Hus was burned (26 July).

shipped.kurz: The council's decrees: Haec sancta and the sentence
shipped.warum: From Mansi's collection (1784), read against the page images with a working translation: Haec sancta, by which the council claimed its power immediately from Christ (6 April 1415); the sentence of 6 July 1415 against Hus as 'Wyclif's disciple' and 'a true and manifest heretic'; and five of the thirty condemned articles.

Five passages from the book the council drew its articles from, in David Schaff's English (1915), read against the page images: the Church of the predestined, Christ nearer than a pope two thousand miles away, the avaricious pope as 'the vicar of Judas', 'to rebel against an erring pope is to obey Christ', and 'no superior is above correction'.

shipped.kurz: Ulrich Richental's chronicle of the council
shipped.warum: The Constance citizen's German chronicle (Buck 1882), read against the page images with a working translation: Hus caught in a haycart, 'why have you broken your safe conduct yourself?', and the king handing the condemned man over 'in our stead'.

planned.kurz: The protest of the Bohemian lords (2 September 1415)
planned.warum: Four hundred and more lords of Bohemia and Moravia seal a letter to the council: Hus was a good and just man, and his death a wrong done to the kingdom.

planned.kurz: Poggio on the death of Jerome of Prague (1416)
planned.warum: A humanist at the council writes to Leonardo Bruni about the eloquence and the burning of Hus's friend, as if he had watched a Roman die.
planned.quelle: Poggio Bracciolini, letter to Leonardo Bruni, 30 May 1416, in a public-domain edition to be identified.

planned.warum: The Prague chronicler of the revolution: the defenestration of 30 July 1419, the Four Articles of Prague, Žižka, the crusade and the battle of Vítkov.
planned.quelle: Vavřinec z Březové, Kronika husitská, ed. J. Goll, Fontes rerum Bohemicarum V (Prague 1893).
